title: High efficiency, Site-specific Transfection of Adherent Cells with siRNA Using Microelectrode Arrays (MEA)
protocol: Sterilize the MEA in an autoclave prior to cell seeding.
Transfer the autoclaved MEA to a laminar flow hood and place it in a standard sterile polystyrene Petri dish.
Turn on the UV light in the laminar flow hood for 20 min before seeding cells.
Cover the Petri dish containing the MEA with sterile aluminum foil while the flow hood is under UV illumination if the MEA is sensitive to UV light.
Harvest cells from a running cell line of adherent mammalian cells using Trypsin/EDTA.
Raise cells to a concentration of 100-200 cells/μl in 1 ml cell media for plating.
Place a 20-30 μl drop of media with cells on the MEA.
Transfer the Petri dish with the MEA to the incubator.
After 2 hr, transfer the Petri dish with the MEA from the incubator to laminar flow hood.
Gently add 400-500 μl of pre-warmed media (37 °C) to the MEA well.
Check under the microscope to ensure that cells are still attached and evenly spread on the MEA surface.
Transfer the MEA back to the incubator.
If cells do not adhere well, treat the MEA surface with cell attachment factors such as fibronectin (10 μg/ml) for 1-2 hr.
Perform 1-2 washes with PBS to remove dead cells.
Replace cell medium every 24-48 hours as needed.
Wait until the culture is at least 80% confluent before proceeding.
Prepare a 1-2 μM siRNA electroporation solution in ice cold electroporation buffer.
Transfer the MEA with cells from the incubator to a sterile laminar flow hood.
Remove the cell medium from the MEA.
Wash the MEA with PBS.
Add 200-400 μl of the ice cold 1 μM siRNA electroporation solution to the well.
Apply anodic square electric pulses to the targeted electrodes using a Pragmatic Instruments 2414A waveform generator.
Connect the waveform generator to a DIP clip via a demultiplexor printed circuit board for electrode selectivity.
Place a steel cathode in the cell media as a reference electrode, ensuring it is 1 mm above the cells without touching the MEA surface.
Use neighboring electrodes as cathode-anode pairs if an external reference electrode is not used.
Transfer the MEA back to the incubator immediately after applying electric pulses.
Incubate the MEA for 5 min.
Replace 75% of the electroporation buffer with pre-warmed (37 °C) cell media.
Conduct fluorescent imaging to confirm delivery of fluorescently tagged siRNA to cells.
Design electroporation experiments for a range of values of pulse amplitude, pulse duration, and number of pulses.
Establish a cell culture on the MEA following the directions outlined in steps 1 and 2.
Prepare a 300-500 μl of 30 μg/ml propidium iodide solution in ice cold electroporation buffer.
Prepare a 400 μl of 4 μM calcein AM solution in PBS.
Transfer the MEA from the incubator to the laminar flow hood.
Remove the cell media from the MEA.
Wash the MEA with PBS.
Add 300-500 μl of ice cold electroporation buffer with PI to the MEA.
Apply electric pulses with desired pulse amplitude and duration to targeted electrodes using the equipment described in step 3.3.
Use either a steel electrode lowered into the electroporation buffer or the neighboring electrode as reference.
Perform multiple experiments by applying pulses of varying amplitudes or durations to different electrodes on the same device.

For example, split 32 electrodes into 8 groups of 4 and stimulate each group with rectangular voltage pulses of 5 msec duration in a range of 3 V-6 V with 0.5 V increments, using one group as control.
Transfer the MEA to the incubator immediately after applying the voltage pulses for 5 minutes.
Gently remove 75% of the electroporation buffer from the MEA well.
Replace removed buffer with warm cell media.
Transfer the MEA back to the incubator.
Incubate cells for 2-4 hours.
Replace cell media in the MEA well with 300-500 μl of a 4 μM Calcein AM solution in PBS.
Transfer the MEA back to the incubator for another 30 minutes.
Wash the MEA well twice with PBS.
Replace the Calcein AM solution in the MEA well with PBS.
Obtain fluorescent images of cells using an optical microscope equipped with filters for PI (Excitation/Emission - 535 nm/617 nm) and Calcein AM (Excitation/Emission - 490 nm/520 nm).
Calculate cell viability as a percentage of the total number of live cells on the electrode.
Calculate electroporation efficiency as a percentage of the total number of PI/siRNA-loaded cells.
